sections.overview: Eumorpha anchemolus is a Neotropical sphinx moth and a congener of E. fasciatus and E. labruscae, described in their profiles.
sections.identification: This large sphinx moth has forewing and hindwing patterning useful for identification; consult the linked regional identification account for detailed marks.
sections.habitat: The moth is recorded from South America north through Central America and Mexico; occasional northern records should not imply a resident range.
sections.diet: Published host records include grape-family vines such as Cissus, Vitis and Ampelopsis.
sections.behavior: BAMONA reports nectar use but provides no flight period, so seasonal activity remains poorly summarized.
sections.reproduction: Caterpillars pupate in shallow chambers or burrows in the soil; detailed egg-laying schedules are not summarized in the sources used.
sections.ecology: The three profiles are congeners, but their recorded larval hosts differ: this species uses the plant groups described above.
sections.conservation: Available regional accounts provide limited species-specific information on population trends or conservation status.
